short.q: Ages: 0 < a ≤ 5 has 10 people, 5 < a ≤ 10 has 25, 10 < a ≤ 20 has 30, 20 < a ≤ 40 has 40. Calculate the frequency densities and estimate the number of people aged between 15 and 30. [4]
In a histogram, the bar for 30 < x ≤ 40 has height 2.4 and the bar for 40 < x ≤ 60 has height 1.5 (frequency density axis). Find the frequency of each class. [2]
Chemistry: Ana scored 58 (mean 50, sd 4). Physics: she scored 70 (mean 60, sd 8). In which subject did she do better compared with the other students? [3]
short.model: Chemistry: (58 − 50) ÷ 4 = 2. Physics: (70 − 60) ÷ 8 = 1.25. Chemistry, because the standardised score is higher.

short.q: Sam ran 100 m in 12.8 s (mean 14.0 s, sd 0.8 s) and 200 m in 26.0 s (mean 28.0 s, sd 1.6 s). In which race did he perform better relative to the others? [3]
short.model: 100 m: (12.8 − 14.0) ÷ 0.8 = −1.5. 200 m: (26.0 − 28.0) ÷ 1.6 = −1.25. The 100 m, because a lower (more negative) standardised score means a faster time.
